chunks: Ahmad b. Ali b. Ibrahim (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrahim b. Hashim, from Hammad b. Isa, from al-Husayn b. al-Mukhtar, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). He said:
One silver coin earned in usury is more grievous in the sight of Allah than thirty acts of fornication, all of them with a mahram such as a maternal aunt or a paternal aunt.

key_terms.درهم: Dirham - a silver coin, the standard unit of currency in early Islamic societies
key_terms.ربا: Usury/interest - the practice of charging interest on loans, absolutely forbidden in Islam
key_terms.محرم: Mahram - a close relative with whom marriage is permanently forbidden

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the severity of usury (riba) compared to other sins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delivers a stark warning about the severity of usury (riba) in Islam, stating that even a single dirham of usury outweighs thirty acts of incestuous fornication in divine judgment. This hadith was transmitted through the well-known narrator Abu Basir and underscores the absolute prohibition of interest-based transactions in Islamic jurisprudence, a subject on which the Quran itself is emphatic (cf. 2:275-279). The hyperbolic comparison is intended to shock the listener into recognizing that economic exploitation through usury is a greater offense against the divine order than even the most severe sexual transgressions.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ahmad b. `Ali b. Ibrahim (rh) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us from his father Ibrhaim b. Hashim from Hammad b. `Isa from al-Husayn b. al-Mukhtar from Abi Basir from Abi `Abdillah (as). He said:
One silver coin [earned] in usury is more significant to Allah than fornicating thirty times with mahrams, like aunts and uncles.
